prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1171; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a low-speed collision in a parking lot. Insured vehicle was stationary and struck on the rear quarter panel by a third-party vehicle reversing out of a space. Both drivers exited and exchanged information. Police not called. Photos of both vehicles requested from insured.

Entry 2: Third-party driver's carrier acknowledged liability in principle. Insured's vehicle inspected at repair facility; damage estimate pending. Claimant reports neck and lower back discomfort following the impact and has retained counsel. Counsel letter of representation received and logged. All further contact to be routed through counsel.

Entry 3: Medical authorization requested through claimant's attorney. Records indicate a diagnosis of lumbar strain with muscle spasm. Treating provider recommends physical therapy and a period of limited lifting. No fracture or disc involvement noted on initial imaging. Claimant reports pain rated moderate and ongoing sleep disruption.

Entry 4: Counsel submitted a demand package including treatment notes, therapy attendance logs, and wage documentation. Claimant reports missed work during the treatment period. Reviewed records with claims supervisor. Requested clarification from counsel on gaps in treatment and on the causal link between the collision and the reported symptoms. Response requested within the standard timeframe.

Entry 5: Counsel responded with supplemental records addressing treatment gaps. Vehicle repair completed and invoice received. Injury claim remains open pending independent medical review and evaluation of the demand. Reserves reviewed and adjusted. Next action: schedule review meeting and confirm file status with counsel.
